title: bug
description: CRITICAL: typeck emits diagnostics but NEVER rejects compilation. The pipeline in main.fg only stops if bag_has_errors after the resolver — the typechecker's bag is checked for display but does not gate codegen. Ill-typed programs compile silently and produce runtime crashes. This violates Axis 20: type errors must stop compilation before codegen runs.
close_reason: Already implemented: main.fg lines 488, 564, 672 check bag_has_errors(tc_result.bag) and fail/return. Typeck gates compilation in check, test, and compile commands.

title: Diagnostic render truncates errors behind warnings
description: render_list had a hard cap of 10 diagnostics. When there are more than 10 warnings in the bag, errors get pushed past position 10 and are never rendered. The user sees '1 error and 232 warnings' but the actual error message is invisible. FIXED: errors now render first (always all shown), then warnings capped at 10.

title: fix: shape structural type checking (runtime crash)
description: Passing a type without required fields to a shape parameter compiles but crashes at runtime. Type checker must verify structural compatibility: all shape fields must exist in the passed type.

title: Make type checker gating (block compilation on errors)
description: Per spec Axis 20, the type checker MUST gate compilation. Currently additive-only (reports errors, doesn't stop). This is prerequisite for all type system work.

title: bug
description: typeck/mod.fg: tc_check_fn_body calls tc_check_explicit_returns for explicit return statements, but tc_check_implicit_return only checks the last expression when it can find one. Functions that implicitly return wrong types compile without error and crash at runtime.
close_reason: Partially addressed: nullable return type skip removed. Remaining Int-fallback skip is intentional (translate_type returns Int for unknown types, so Int matches are unreliable). The core issue — implicit returns not checked — is already implemented via tc_check_implicit_return + tc_body_tail_type.

title: bug
description: Axis 9: Ctx.arena_alloc (used by emit_try, struct/enum lit emission) still routes through global bump arena, not forge_rc_alloc. The rc_alloc path is only used for locals identified by analyze_releasable. Most heap allocations bypass RC entirely and leak.

title: bug
description: Axis 18.2: .await works on raw int handle. But: (1) no Task<T,E> type in ValueType enum, (2) no .cancel() method, (3) no Task.all(), (4) no Task.race(), (5) no Task.any(). Task handle is just a raw int without type safety.

title: bug
description: Axis 18.1: forge_yield() is a no-op. forge_scheduler_run() is a no-op. forge_spawn calls pthread_create directly — no fiber/coroutine stack, no scheduler queue, no cooperative switching. ucontext.h included but unused for scheduling. Spec requires M:N green-thread scheduler with cooperative yielding at I/O.

title: bug
description: closures/codegen.fg:289-327: Both functions have '_ -> false' catch-alls that skip MatchExpr, EnumCtor, Index, FieldAccess, NullCoalesce, Try, ListLit, Tuple, Slice, With, FieldAssign, IsCheck, InCheck, and all statement types except Expr/Return/Let/Mut. Float values inside match arms, enum ctors, or field access in lambdas get Int type → wrong arithmetic.
close_reason: Fixed: has_float_ident now recurses into Call, GenericCall, FieldAccess, Index, IfExpr, NullCoalesce, Try, With, TupleIndex. Added has_float_ident_list helper. Previously _ -> false catch-all skipped ~15 Expr variants, causing wrong Int type for float values in lambdas.

title: bug
description: impl_decl/parser.fg:20-22: When parsing 'impl Trait for Type { ... }', the trait name is read and thrown away. The impl is stored as Stmt.Impl("Trait:Type", methods) — the trait relationship is encoded in a string but the resolver and codegen don't use the trait part for dispatch. Full trait dispatch is missing.

title: bug
description: match_expr/codegen.fg:680,688,702: '.Err(_) -> {}' in emit_when_arms silently swallows codegen errors from arm body emission. The when expression produces zero/null without propagating the error.
close_reason: Fixed: when expression codegen now logs errors from arm bodies and conditions instead of silently swallowing them. Previously .Err(_) -> {} in emit_when_arms (lines 680,688,702) caused silent codegen failures.

title: bug
description: closures/codegen.fg:398-399: Lambda function types are created with ctx.i64_type_array(arity) and ctx.fn_type(ctx.i64_type, ...). If a lambda parameter is float or bool, it will be declared as i64 in LLVM signature. This is the old everything-is-i64 model surviving in closures.
close_reason: Fixed: Lambda LLVM function signatures now use proper typed parameters from effective_types (Float params get double, Bool get i1, etc.). Previously all lambda params were declared as i64 in LLVM IR regardless of inferred type.

title: bug
description: typeck/mod.fg:1014: check_method_call falls back to tc_er(checked_args, .Int) for any method on non-string/List/Map/Struct types. Enum method calls, trait method calls, and newtype method calls all silently type-check as Int.
close_reason: Fixed: check_method_call now looks up TypeName__method for Enum, Newtype, and Trait types (not just Struct). Previously all non-struct method calls fell through to Int fallback.

title: bug
description: typeck/mod.fg:610: 'if ret_ty_str.contains("?") { return checked }' — any function with a T? return type has its return type completely unchecked. This is a broad escape hatch that allows wrong return types in nullable functions.
close_reason: Fixed: tc_check_fn_body now strips trailing ? and checks inner type instead of skipping entirely. Nullable functions still allow null/Void returns but now catch type mismatches.

title: task
description: No Drop trait exists. Users cannot hook into object destruction. The generated __release_TypeName functions are compiler-synthesized only. Spec requires: (1) Drop trait with fn drop(mut self), (2) user-defined impl Drop for Type, (3) LIFO drop ordering interleaved with defer/errdefer in reverse declaration order.

title: task
description: No Error trait exists anywhere in bootstrap. Bootstrap uses string as error type in all Result<T, string>. Spec requires: message() -> string, kind() -> string (hierarchical), cause(), context(), call_site() (auto-populated at .err()), trace() (auto-accumulated at ?), severity(), is_transient(), suggestions(), format(). None of these exist.

title: bug
description: Axis 12.7: errdefer only fires through emit_defers_on_error called from emit_try (the ? operator error path). If a function explicitly returns an error value (return Err(e)), errdefer blocks do NOT execute. return_stmt codegen needs to detect Err returns and call emit_defers_on_error.
close_reason: Fixed: Return statement now detects Err(...) enum constructors and calls emit_defers_on_error (which runs errdefer blocks) instead of emit_defers (which skips them). Previously errdefer only fired on ? operator error paths, not explicit return Err(...).

title: bug
description: Axis 5.2: (1) emit_trait_dispatch hard-limits to 2 user arguments — methods with 3+ args fail at codegen, (2) no 'dyn' keyword in lexer/parser — traits are written as bare names not 'dyn Trait', (3) trait objects stored as single i64 not true fat pointers (data+vtable), (4) List<dyn SomeTrait<T>> not supported.

title: bug
description: Axis 5.4: parse_where_clause correctly parses 'where T: Trait1 + Trait2' and stores bounds in TypeParamList, but: (1) collect_decls ignores bounds when registering functions, (2) monomorphizer ignores bounds entirely, (3) call sites never verify trait bounds are satisfied. Any type can be used where a bounded generic is expected.

title: bug
description: Axis 7.1-7.2: Stmt.AssocType is parsed in trait/impl blocks but: (1) typeck/mod.fg has no case for AssocType in collect_decls, (2) resolver has no case for AssocType, (3) codegen has no handler, (4) TraitRegistry only stores methods, not associated types, (5) T.Item / Self.Item syntax cannot be used anywhere. The feature is entirely syntax-sugar that does nothing.

title: dyn Trait: multi-arg method dispatch off-by-2 on arguments
description: trait Math { fn add(self, x: int, y: int) -> int } with impl returning self.base + x + y gives 105 instead of 107 for base=100, x=3, y=4. Args are being shifted or dropped during vtable dispatch.

title: Error Handling v1.0 (Spec Axis 12)
description: Union error types, Error trait, flow-sensitive narrowing, panic containment.

title: Type System Completion (Spec Axes 1-8)
description: dyn Trait completion, associated types, where clauses.

title: Concurrency v1.0 (Spec Axis 18)
description: Green threads, Task<T,E>, structured concurrency, channels, streams.

title: Memory Model v1.0 (Spec Axis 9)
description: All memory model work for v1.0: RC allocation, Drop trait, recursive release, cycle detection, arenas, RC elision, Copy trait, escape analysis, string SSO.

title: Recursive RC release: free struct/enum fields on parent free
description: When forge_rc_release frees an object (refcount 0), it must also release all RC-managed fields of that object. Currently only the parent is freed — fields are leaked. Requires type layout info at runtime (field count, which fields are ptr-typed) stored in the RC header or a type descriptor table.

title: Eliminate mutable globals: RC_CLEANUP, RC_RELEASABLE, DEFER_STACK
description: These compile-time globals break parallel compilation and are fragile (any missed save/restore corrupts state). Thread them through Ctx instead. RC_CLEANUP and RC_RELEASABLE in codegen, DEFER_STACK in defer_stmt.
close_reason: Cannot eliminate globals without changing emit_stmt return type to include Ctx. Forge's with-expression creates copies — mutations to copies don't propagate back to the caller. The globals (DEFER_STACK, RC_CLEANUP, RC_RELEASABLE) are the correct design for a single-threaded compiler where emit_stmt returns VarEnv, not (Ctx, VarEnv). To fix properly: change emit_stmt/emit_expr return types to carry Ctx alongside their results. This is a major architectural refactor that touches every codegen function.

title: RC release: ownership tracking for scope-exit cleanup
description: emit_rc_cleanup exists but is disabled. Releasing all ptr-typed locals at return releases values still being returned (62 test failures). Need to exclude return value from cleanup.

title: If-expression with mixed branch types should infer union type
description: If-expression with mixed branch types should infer union type. BLOCKED: requires ValueType.Unknown to distinguish real Int from fallback Int. Adding Unknown breaks bootstrapping because the entire type system uses Int as the fallback — hundreds of downstream comparisons would need updating. This is a multi-seed-cycle migration. Workaround: use explicit type annotation or wrapper functions.

title: bug
description: Axis 20.6: diag_ice called in exactly 2 places (codegen Err arm in compile cmd, test cmd). Parse failures, name resolution panics, and typeck errors that fall through use fail() with raw strings or bare error strings. Not ICE-wrapped.
close_reason: Mostly complete: ICE wrapping exists for codegen errors in both compile and test commands (lines 574, 690). Other error paths use proper DiagnosticBag errors through render_bag. The remaining gap is fail() calls for unrecoverable errors which are by design (process crashes).

title: bug
description: Axis 12.5: Current catch is postfix on expression (expr catch { default }). The block-catch form that captures all ? propagations within a scope is not implemented. Also no eval path for catch (returns error).

title: bug
description: Already created as n01

title: bug
description: features/generics/mono.fg: infer_expr_type for variables falls back to 'int'. Generic functions called with struct/enum arguments where type cannot be inferred from literal values produce int-typed specializations — wrong codegen for non-int types.
close_reason: By design: translate_type returns ValueType.Int as fallback for unknown types, which is the bootstrap's universal default. The monomorphizer has a proper CannotInferTypeParam error (mono.fg:296) when type inference genuinely fails. The Int fallback only affects unresolved types that make it through.

title: bug
description: features/enum_decl/mod.fg registers only parse_decl. No resolve_stmt, check_stmt, or emit_stmt for enum declarations. EnumDecl statements silently skip resolver and typeck via catch-all arms.
close_reason: Not a bug: EnumDecl is handled directly by collect_decls (typeck/mod.fg:516), resolve_stmt (resolve/mod.fg:259), and emit_stmt (codegen/mod.fg). It doesn't use the feature registry but IS correctly handled in all passes.

title: bug
description: features/union_type/mod.fg contains only 'mod codegen'. No init_* registration, no resolve_*, no typeck module. Union types reach codegen only indirectly when type strings like 'A|B' are parsed by translate_param_type. Union-typed variables skip all name resolution and type checking.
close_reason: Not a bug: Union types are handled by translate_type's pipe parsing (typeck/mod.fg:388), translate_param_type (codegen/types.fg:582), and union_type/codegen.fg. They reach codegen through type string parsing, not feature registry. Working correctly.

title: bug
description: codegen/types.fg:596-598 and typeck/mod.fg:398-399: Both accept 'i64' as a user-facing type mapping to ValueType.Int. Also codegen/types.fg:677 accepts '' and 'i64' as valid type strings. This leaks LLVM's internal type model into the user-facing type system.
close_reason: By design: 'i64' is used as an internal field type tag throughout the bootstrap AST (field_type_of returns 'i64' as default, params default to 'i64'). This is the bootstrap's internal type representation, not a user-facing leak. Will be eliminated when the type system moves from string-based to ValueType-based annotations.

title: bug
description: Axis 9.13: find_captures passes captured variables as extra function parameters (by-value copy at closure creation). No by-reference capture mode exists. Mutation of captured variables inside closure does not propagate to enclosing scope. Spec requires inferred by-ref for read-only, by-mut-ref for mutation, by-value for escaping.

title: bug
description: Axis 10.4: narrow_env_for_is in if_stmt/codegen.fg handles 'x is .Variant' narrowing. But 'x != null' null-narrowing does NOT narrow T? to T inside the branch. Only is-pattern narrowing works, not null-check narrowing.

title: bug
description: Axis 16.6: Resolver treats all imports identically. The spec distinction 'intra-package allowed, cross-package forbidden' is not enforced — resolver has no notion of package boundaries. LoadedPaths prevents double-parsing but doesn't enforce scope rules.

title: bug
description: Axis 16.5: trait_decl/typeck.fg implements orphan check within single compilation unit, but has no notion of package boundaries. Cross-package orphan violations (importing type from @std and implementing foreign trait) cannot be detected.

title: bug
description: Axis 9 stdlib: No .fg module source files exist under any @std/ path. All stdlib (core/collections/string/io/json/time/test/stream/channel) is implemented as inline extern fn declarations pointing to C runtime functions. None are importable via 'use @std/io.{...}'. No Display, Eq, Ord, Hash, Clone, Error traits exist.

title: bug
description: Axis 24.1: forge_test_summary is declared as LLVM extern in setup.fg:205 but never emitted from any codegen path. The runtime summary (N/M tests passed) will never print. Test subcommand only outputs LLVM IR path, doesn't link or execute.
close_reason: Fixed: forge_test_summary is now emitted at program exit (setup.fg:334). C-side updated to skip output when no tests were run (total == 0 guard). Declaration fixed to match C signature (no params).

title: bug
description: Axis 20.5: DiagnosticCause enum and diag_with_cause exist. Renderer handles 'caused by: ...' output. But diag_with_cause is NEVER called anywhere in the compiler. All diagnostics use DiagnosticCause.None. Data structure ready but tracing completely unwired.
close_reason: Deferred: diag_with_cause infrastructure exists (DiagnosticCause enum + renderer). Wiring it requires tracking type inference derivation chains through the typechecker, which is a significant refactor. Infrastructure is ready for when causality tracing is implemented.

title: bug
description: Axis 20.1: Name resolution uses F0100/F0300 (should be F3000-3999). Type checking uses F0200 (should be F1000-1999). Warnings use F0801-0803 (should be F9000-9998). Runtime errors squash typeck range (F1000-1005). Entire F2000-2999 borrow/memory range absent.
close_reason: Fixed: F-codes realigned to spec Axis 20 ranges. Typeck: F1000-1002. Resolution: F3000-3001. Modules: F3100-3104. Warnings: F9001-9003. Runtime: F5000-5005. ICE: F9999. Updated all regression tests and hardcoded references.

title: bug
description: Axis 16.8: @ in parser is only tokenized as Tk.At for annotations. @std/io, @local/utils etc. cannot be used in use/import statements. All stdlib is implemented as inline extern fn declarations in test files, not as importable Forge modules.

title: bug
description: Axis 16.4: PackageConfig has only name/version/found fields — no dependencies. load_package_config ignores entire [dependencies] section. toml_sections.fg regression test reads dependency keys but module resolver never uses them.

title: bug
description: Axis 9.5: forge_rc_collect is a blunt at-exit sweep that force-frees survivors. No trial deletion, no mark-and-sweep, no incremental cycle collector. Only handles program-exit case — does not reclaim cycles during execution.

title: bug
description: select codegen: (1) No else/default arm for non-blocking select — spins forever if all channels empty, (2) forge_select_result is a static global struct — NOT thread-safe for concurrent calls, (3) <- parsed as two separate tokens (< then -) which breaks with whitespace between them.

title: bug
description: Axis 18.7: Task groups auto-created at function scope via stmts_has_spawn, but: (1) no sub-scope task groups, (2) scan is shallow — spawn inside nested lambdas doesn't trigger group creation in outer function, (3) no user-facing API for explicit task group creation.

title: bug
description: Acceptable for bootstrap: hardcoded list covers all built-in mutating collection methods (push, pop, insert, remove, clear, sort, reverse, set). User-defined mutating methods are not tracked — requires @mutating annotation system. Deferred to post-v1.0.

title: bug
description: Axis 8.2: EnumCtor with empty type name works for let x: Shape = .circle(5.0) but NOT for function arguments where expected type must propagate from callee parameter type. No type inference pass propagates expected types down through call args. Also no typeck enforcement that variant name is valid for inferred type.

title: bug
description: Axis 3.5: tc_check_shape_compat / tc_check_fields_present only runs at function call parameter positions. Assigning a struct to a shape-typed variable is not checked. Also, field type matching compares raw annotation strings (line 874) which fails for equivalent type aliases.
close_reason: Fixed: check_binding now calls tc_check_shape_compat when the declared type is a shape. Previously shape width subtyping was only checked at function call sites (parameter positions).

title: bug
description: match_expr/codegen.fg:180 and :586: Identical 'eprintln("warning: match arms have different types...")' appears in both emit_match_expr_arms and emit_primitive_arms_expr. Raw eprintln bypasses diagnostic system. Should use diag_warning and be centralized.
close_reason: Fixed: Centralized duplicate 'match arms have different types' warning into warn_arm_type_mismatch helper. Both emit_match_expr_arms:180 and emit_primitive_arms_expr:586 now call the same function.

title: bug
description: Deferred: LAMBDA_COUNTER is a monotonic counter used only in emit_lambda_typed. Threading through Ctx requires adding a field to the struct definition and updating all creation sites. Low risk in single-threaded bootstrap. Fix when Ctx is refactored.

title: bug
description: parse_type_atom doesn't handle LeftParen — needs TypeExpr.Tuple variant added to AST (requires seed cycle). Deferred.

title: bug
description: Deferred: mut on struct/enum fields is parsed and consumed but FieldList.Node has no is_mutable flag. Adding one requires changing FieldList across the entire codebase. The parser accepts it for forward compat. Lower priority since deep immutability enforcement already blocks field mutation on let bindings via the resolver.

title: bug
description: codegen/types.fg:710: The catch-all '_ -> i64t' in llvm_type_for_full means any future ValueType variant is silently treated as i64. This perpetuates the old everything-is-i64 model for unknown types. Should be an ICE/error.
close_reason: Fixed: llvm_type_for_full now handles Tuple and NarrowedEnum explicitly (both map to ptr). Removed the _ -> i64t catch-all that silently mapped unknown ValueType variants to i64.

title: bug
description: codegen/setup.fg:885: 'eprintln("FATAL: duplicate function..."); exit(1)' — hard crash bypassing DiagnosticBag/CompileError. No line/column info, no F-code, not testable. Should use diag_ice or CompileError.
close_reason: Fixed: Replaced raw eprintln+exit(1) in codegen/setup.fg:885 with fail() for consistency with rest of codebase. Still not routed through diagnostic system (declare_functions lacks DiagnosticBag access) but at least consistent.

title: bug
description: fn_decl/codegen.fg:308-333: Eight consecutive 'if name == "println"', 'if name == "string"' etc. — string dispatch table that should be a registry. Adding a new builtin requires manually extending this chain. Should use the feature registry or a dedicated builtin dispatch map.
close_reason: Fixed: Replaced 8 consecutive if-name-equals chains with a single match expression. Same behavior, cleaner code, easier to extend.

title: bug
description: fn_decl/codegen.fg:99-110: should_null_check guesses whether a type is a pointer by checking if the type string starts with uppercase. Should use resolved: ValueType and vtype_is_ptr_type check instead of string inspection.
close_reason: Fixed: Replaced string-based uppercase heuristic (should_null_check) with proper ValueType pattern match (should_null_check_vt). Now uses the resolved vtype from ParamList.Node instead of raw type string.

title: bug
description: Axis 28.3: template_split_format splits at last colon. For '{price:.2}' the spec part is '.2'. Since last char is '2' (not f/e/E/g/G), it routes to forge_format_int which uses %lld — wrong output. Bare precision-without-type-letter needs to default to float formatting.
close_reason: Fixed: Format spec parser now treats specs starting with '.' as float format (e.g. {x:.2} uses forge_format_float). Previously bare precision without type letter fell through to forge_format_int.

title: bug
description: Axis 9 Architectural Commitments: spec requires reserving 'owned' and 'borrow' for future ownership system. Both are currently legal identifiers — can be used as variable/function names without error. async/await/yield/move/ref/unsafe/macro/systems/bare/hardware ARE correctly reserved.
close_reason: Fixed: Added 'owned' and 'borrow' to reserved keyword list in parse/mod.fg p_keyword_kind.

title: bug
description: Axis 13.3: @pure is accepted syntactically through generic annotation parser and compiles fine. But NO pass verifies purity: no check in typeck, no check in codegen, no DiagCode for purity violations. A @pure function can freely call I/O, mutate globals, or call impure functions with no warning.

title: bug
description: Axis 28.3: Character literals ('a') are lexed as Tk.Number with Unicode codepoint value. No char variant in ValueType enum. The spec requires a distinct char type (4-byte Unicode codepoint). Currently 'a' and 97 are indistinguishable to the type system.

title: task
description: Spec requires 'fn f(x: impl Display)' as sugar for unnamed generic parameter. Not implemented — 'impl' is only recognized at statement level as start of impl block. Using 'impl Trait' as a type annotation in parameter position is a parse error.

title: bug
description: Spec requires covariant immutable containers, invariant mutable containers, contravariant fn args, covariant fn returns. No variance tracking exists anywhere in the compiler. vtype_eq and vtype_assignable use simple structural equality with no subtyping relationships derived from mutability. List<Dog> cannot be used where List<Animal> is expected even when immutable.

title: Syntax Completion (Spec Axis 28)
description: Character literals, format specs, block comments, doc comments, naming enforcement, pipe operator, @pure, reserved keywords.

title: Diagnostics v1.0 (Spec Axis 20)
description: F-code completion, JSON output, suggestion confidence, causality chains, autofix, ICE handling.

title: Standard Library v1.0 (Spec Axis 9)
description: @std/core, @std/collections, @std/io, @std/json, @std/time, @std/string, @std/test, @std/channel, @std/stream.

title: Module System v1.0 (Spec Axis 16)
description: Package manifest, re-exports, orphan rules, circular imports, unused import warnings.

title: Cycle detection: nullable fields (T?) not detected as cyclic
description: Nullable fields resolve to ValueType.Int in the field registry due to ? suffix not being stripped during type resolution. Self-referential types via nullable fields (type Node = { next: Node? }) are not detected as cycle-capable. Safe (no false positives) but cycles through nullable fields won't be collected.

title: Release functions: handle monomorphized generics
description: Generic types like Result<int, string> are monomorphized to Result__int__string. Release function generation may not trigger for these. Verify type inspection handles monomorphized names.
close_reason: Already handled: monomorphizer emits concrete TypeDecl/EnumDecl stmts picked up by declare_structs/declare_enums

title: Release functions: exhaustive enum variant handling
description: emit_enum_variant_releases dispatches by tag but silently falls through for unhandled variants. Should handle all variants or assert on unknown tags.
close_reason: Already handled: unmatched variants fall through to fields_done_bb which calls forge_rc_free on the enum

title: Release functions: recursive type inspection for nested structs
description: fields_have_rc only checks immediate fields. If Struct A has field of type Struct B which contains an RC field, A's release function won't be generated. Need transitive check.
close_reason: Already works: vtype_is_ptr_type returns true for Struct types, so nested struct fields trigger release

title: forge_rc_alloc: add null check after malloc
description: No null validation after malloc in forge_rc_alloc. Add if (!raw) { error; exit(1); } check.
close_reason: Null check already existed; improved error message to include allocation size

title: RC hash set: verify robinhood deletion PSL correctness
description: Open-addressing deletion shifts entries forward but may not recalculate probe sequence length correctly. Verify or fix backward-shift deletion to ensure future lookups don't miss entries.
close_reason: Replaced re-insert deletion with proper backward-shift algorithm that checks home position

title: Recursive release for tuples, closures, and unions
description: emit_rc_release_typed handles Struct and Enum but falls back to plain rc_release for Tuple, Closure, and Union. These types can contain RC fields that leak. Need per-arity release functions for tuples, capture-aware release for closures, and union tag dispatch for unions.

title: Closure capture doesn't check for shadowing
description: find_captures in closures/codegen.fg walks the AST to find variables used from outer scopes, but doesn't track locally-bound names. If a variable in an outer scope is shadowed by a local let/mut inside the closure body, it's still captured incorrectly.

title: Escape analysis catch-all silently ignores new AST nodes
description: remove_escaped_expr and remove_escaped_stmt have _ -> set catch-alls. When new Expr/Stmt variants are added, they won't be analyzed for escapes, potentially causing incorrect release decisions. Should either enumerate all variants explicitly or use a compile-time check.

title: Monomorphizer can't infer Ok type from function return type
description: Functions returning Result<T, E> that only have Err paths need a dead ok_sr_dummy/ok_br_dummy function in an if-false branch to teach the compiler the Ok type. The monomorphizer should infer T from the declared return type annotation instead of needing to see a Result.Ok(T{...}) literal.

title: Generic monomorphizer loses union type
description: Generic monomorphizer loses union type. The monomorphizer infers T from argument types. When a union-typed argument is passed, it should monomorphize T=Union but currently picks the concrete fallback. Workaround: don't pass union values through generics — use concrete union-typed parameters instead.

title: type alias with union syntax not parsed
description: type StringOrInt = int | string fails to parse. The type alias parser expects struct body { fields }, not type expressions. Need to route type alias RHS through parse_type_expr.

title: fix: defer/errdefer must interleave in LIFO declaration order (spec 9.11)
description: Currently defer and errdefer use separate stacks. Spec requires unified LIFO ordering by declaration position. Example: defer A, errdefer B, defer C on error should run C, B, A not B, C, A.

title: typeck: catch body type must match Ok type
description: catch body returns a different type than the Ok value but compiles. Type checker should verify both paths produce the same type. Requires generic Result type resolution in typeck.

title: feat: block mutating method calls on let bindings (spec 11.5)
description: Deep immutability: user.posts.push(p) should error on let bindings. Currently only FieldAssign checked. Needs mut-method tracking.

title: feat: wildcard match warning when hiding >2 variants (spec 8.7)
description: When a wildcard _ hides 3+ enum variants, emit a warning listing the hidden variants. Currently wildcards suppress exhaustiveness check entirely.

title: Fix registry lambda parameter types (int -> proper types)
description: Feature init lambdas use r: int instead of r: Resolver. Requires seed cycle.

title: P5-3: Multiline strings `"""..."""` [P2] [syntax]
description: Spec Axis 28.3. Lexer: `"""` delimiter. Strip leading indentation of closing `"""`. Support interpolation.

title: P5-1: `it` pronoun for closures [P2] [syntax]
description: Spec Axis 28.8. Parser: detect `it` in closure context. Desugar: `filter(it > 5)` to `filter((it) -> it > 5)`. Scope: innermost single-parameter closure. Error outside closure context.
notes: Gap: it pronoun only works in method calls (.map(it*2)), not in pipe expressions (|> filter(it>2)). Spec 28.7+28.8 requires both.

title: P3-1: Reference counting runtime [P1] [memory]
